mechanism_narrative: Declining PARKS mobility over the past four weeks signals exhaustion of outdoor recreation substitution. Consumers will redirect leisure spending back to indoor retail venues, driving RETAIL_REC upward over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS declined from 23.6% to -0.4% over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the mean of the prior 28 days, or PARKS continues declining below -5%.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent RESIDENTIAL elevation (5-11% above baseline) combined with stagnant WORKPLACES (around -30%) indicates sustained remote work and home-based consumption. This regime suppresses retail foot traffic, keeping RETAIL_REC depressed over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES remains below -25% AND RESIDENTIAL remains above 5%
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES at -27.4%, RESIDENTIAL at 5.3% in t-0w
failure_condition: WORKPLACES rises above -20% or RESIDENTIAL falls below 3%, or RETAIL_REC increases by more than 5 percentage points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has remained severely depressed (around -40%) for four consecutive weeks, indicating sustained restrictions on public transportation or consumer avoidance. This constraint on mobility access will prevent RETAIL_REC recovery over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -35% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: TRANSIT rises above -30% or RETAIL_REC increases by more than 3 percentage points from current baseline.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has declined monotonically from -9.3% to -16.4% over four weeks, signaling reduced essential-goods shopping frequency. This indicates consumers are consolidating trips and reducing overall mobility engagement, which will suppress RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls below -15% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases above -25% or GROCERY_PHARM rebounds above -12%.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of declining PARKS (from 23.6% to -0.4%) and stagnant RETAIL_REC (around -30%) suggests consumers are neither substituting to outdoor nor indoor leisure. A threshold reversal in PARKS (crossing above 5%) will trigger reallocation of leisure spending to retail venues, lifting RETAIL_REC within one week.
failure_condition: PARKS does not rise above 5% or RETAIL_REC does not increase within one week of PARKS crossing 5%.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-July timing (t-0w = 2020-07-15) marks the onset of summer retail seasonality. Despite current suppression, seasonal demand for apparel and outdoor goods will drive RETAIL_REC upward over the next four weeks independent of mobility constraints.
evidence_refs: fact:Decision time point is 2020-07-15, mid-summer period
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the prior 28-day mean, or summer seasonal patterns do not manifest.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has stabilized around -27% to -30% over four weeks without further decline. This stabilization signals policy acceptance of current remote-work levels. If WORKPLACES remains stable (within ±3 points), RETAIL_REC will remain suppressed as the remote-work regime persists over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES change by less than 3 percentage points week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: WORKPLACES rises above -20% or RETAIL_REC increases by more than 4 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: A three-way interaction among TRANSIT (severely constrained at -40%), WORKPLACES (depressed at -27%), and RESIDENTIAL (elevated at 5.3%) creates a mobility trap. Consumers lack transit access to reach retail, work-from-home reduces incidental shopping, and home-based consumption substitutes for retail. This compound effect will keep RETAIL_REC depressed over the next four weeks unless all three conditions reverse simultaneously.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT below -35% AND WORKPLACES below -25% AND RESIDENTIAL above 4%
evidence_refs: fact:All three conditions met in t-0w
failure_condition: Any one of the three conditions reverses (TRANSIT above -35%, WORKPLACES above -25%, or RESIDENTIAL below 4%), or RETAIL_REC increases by more than 2 percentage points.
